nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The opt\-in cache affects PyTorch GEMM workflows that use discrete weights\. Fix the fused grouped MLP's stale scales during graph replay before merging.

Findings

1.  **Graphs read old weight scales** ▶ 2.  **Unused GPU buffers stay alive** ▶

Summary

Adds opt-in caching through `NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE` to avoid repeatedly swizzling gathered NVFP4 weight scales. - GEMMs reuse swizzled NVFP4 scales after each parameter gather. - Fused grouped MLPs reuse packed pointers for discrete weights.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Weight all-gather] --> B[post_all_gather_processing] B --> C[Refresh weight-owned scale buffers] C --> D[general_gemm and grouped GEMM] B --> E[Advance host generation] E --> F[Fused MLP Python cache check] F --> G[Allocate swizzled scales on a miss] F --> H[Reuse scales on a hit] G --> I[Fused MLP GEMM] H --> I J[Compute-only graph replay] --> K[Read captured scale buffers] K --> I ``` Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[PyTorch\] Cache GEMM-swizzled scales of ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/ac475f2c982552396cd678b26cd861e195ac5cee) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Graphs read old weight scales** With `NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE=1`, warming up the fused grouped MLP before capturing a compute-only CUDA graph makes this branch return cached scales without capturing a swizzle. After weights change through `post_all_gather_processing`, replay still reads the old scales, producing wrong outputs and gradients. The host-side generation check does not run during replay, and the gather hook only refreshes the separate `_gsw_view` buffers. Refresh the buffers used by the captured MLP in place, or keep the swizzle in the graph. Add a replay test using the real fused MLP path; the mocked helper test cannot catch this. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch tensor and operator abstractions](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-tensors-and-ops.md)

+_DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE: dict = {}
+
+
+def _swizzle_pack_discrete(datas, scales, fmt, device):
+    """``swizzle_scales_and_pack_ptrs_for_discrete_weights``, cached until the weights change.
+
+    With ``NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE=1``, expert weights are assumed to change only at a
+    parameter all-gather (``post_all_gather_processing``), so the swizzled scales and packed
+    pointer arrays are reused by every microbatch until the next one. In a CUDA graph that
+    also captures the all-gather, the first use after it is captured and recomputes the
+    cached buffers on every replay.
+    """
+    fn = tex.grouped_mlp_experimental.swizzle_scales_and_pack_ptrs_for_discrete_weights
+    if not nvfp4_weight_swizzle_cache_enabled():
+        return fn(datas, scales, fmt, device)
+    gen = param_gather_generation()
+    key = (
+        fmt,
+        tuple(t.data_ptr() for t in datas),
+        tuple(t.data_ptr() for t in scales),
+    )
+    hit = _DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE.get(key)
+    if hit is not None and hit[0] == gen:
+        return hit[1]

nodes.body: **Unused GPU buffers stay alive** `_DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE` keeps every distinct pointer key for the life of the process. Each value owns GPU scale and pointer buffers, but no entry is removed when its weights die. The fused MLP also calls this helper for BF16 expert weights that it quantizes afresh each forward. New allocation addresses leave old GPU buffers retained, including after a model is deleted. Tie entries to the owning weights or otherwise bound and clean up the cache without breaking captured graphs.

@@ -466,6 +466,12 @@ GEMM Configuration
    :Default: ``0``
    :Description: Enable multi-atomic mode for AllGather with atomic GEMM using P2P communication. When set to ``1``, uses ``userbuffers_sendrecv_multiatomic`` for communication during atomic GEMM overlap with AllGather operations. This disables copy engine (CE) usage and enables push mode for userbuffers. This is an advanced optimization for tensor-parallel communication-computation overlap.
 
+.. envvar:: NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE
+
+   :Type: ``int`` (0 or 1)
+   :Default: ``0``
+   :Description: Cache GEMM-swizzled scale factors of NVFP4 primary weights that are refreshed by ``post_all_gather_processing`` (e.g. Megatron-Core's distributed optimizer with FP4 parameter all-gather). These weights keep compact scales, so without the cache every GEMM that reads them swizzles the weight scales again, once per microbatch. With the cache, the scales are swizzled once per all-gather into persistent buffers that ``general_gemm``, the grouped GEMM with discrete weights and the fused grouped MLP reuse; CUDA graphs keep reading valid scales on replay. The cache assumes such weights change only through ``post_all_gather_processing``: a weight modified in any other way keeps using stale scales until the next call.
+

+# Copyright (c) 2022-2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+"""Tests for NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE.
+
+NVFP4 primary weights refreshed by ``post_all_gather_processing`` keep compact scales.
+With the cache enabled, their GEMM-swizzled scales are built once per all-gather and
+reused by ``general_gemm``, the grouped GEMM with discrete weights and the fused grouped
+MLP. These tests check that (a) cached GEMMs are bit-identical to uncached ones and launch
+fewer swizzle kernels, (b) the cache follows weight updates made through
+``post_all_gather_processing``, and (c) a captured CUDA graph reads the refreshed scales."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import transformer_engine.pytorch as te
+import transformer_engine_torch as tex
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.cpp_extensions import gemm as gemm_mod
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.cpp_extensions import general_gemm
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.ops.fused import grouped_mlp as grouped_mlp_mod
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor import utils as tensor_utils
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.grouped_tensor import GroupedTensor
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.nvfp4_tensor import NVFP4Quantizer
+
+recipe_available, reason_for_no_recipe = te.is_nvfp4_available(return_reason=True)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not recipe_available, reason=reason_for_no_recipe)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def swizzle_cache(monkeypatch):
+    """Toggle the cache; tests switch it off to compute uncached references."""
+
+    def set_enabled(enabled):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(tensor_utils, "_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE", enabled)
+
+    set_enabled(True)
+    yield set_enabled
+
+
+def _swizzle_kernel_count(fn):
+    with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
+        fn()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return sum(1 for e in prof.events() if "swizzle" in e.name)
+
+
+def _make_weights(num, n, k):
+    quantizer = NVFP4Quantizer(rowwise=True, columnwise=True, with_2d_quantization=True)
+    weights = [
+        quantizer(torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)) for _ in range(num)
+    ]
+    for w in weights:
+        assert not w._with_gemm_swizzled_scales
+    return weights
+
+
+def _update_weights(weights):
+    """Simulate an optimizer step plus parameter all-gather."""
+    for w in weights:
+        w.quantize_(torch.randn(w.shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    tensor_utils.post_all_gather_processing(weights)
+
+
+def _quantized_input(m, k):
+    quantizer = NVFP4Quantizer(rowwise=True, columnwise=True)
+    return quantizer(torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+
+
+def test_general_gemm(swizzle_cache):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    (weight,) = _make_weights(1, 512, 1024)
+    x = _quantized_input(256, 1024)
+
+    def gemm():
+        return general_gemm(weight, x, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)[0]
+
+    swizzle_cache(False)
+    ref = gemm()
+    swizzle_cache(True)
+    out = gemm()  # marks the weight
+    assert weight._gsw_wanted
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    tensor_utils.post_all_gather_processing([weight])
+    assert weight._gsw_view is not None
+    torch.testing.assert_close(gemm(), ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    _update_weights([weight])
+    swizzle_cache(False)
+    ref2 = gemm()
+    swizzle_cache(True)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(gemm(), ref2, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert not torch.equal(ref, ref2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["TN", "NN"])
+def test_grouped_gemm_discrete_weights(swizzle_cache, layout):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_groups, n, k = 4, 512, 1024
+    m_splits = (256, 0, 128, 384)
+    weights = _make_weights(num_groups, n, k)
+
+    first_dims = torch.tensor(m_splits, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+    m_total = sum(m_splits)
+    in_features = k if layout == "TN" else n
+    out_features = n if layout == "TN" else k
+    x = torch.randn(m_total, in_features, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    x_quantizer = NVFP4Quantizer(
+        rowwise=True, columnwise=True, with_rht=True, with_post_rht_amax=True
+    )
+    x_quantizer.optimize_for_gemm = True
+    grouped_x = tex.group_quantize(x, x_quantizer, num_groups, first_dims)
+
+    def make_out():
+        return GroupedTensor.make_grouped_tensor(
+            num_tensors=num_groups,
+            first_dims=first_dims,
+            last_dims=None,
+            logical_first_dim=m_total,
+            logical_last_dim=out_features,
+            quantizer=None,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+
+    def gemm(out):
+        gemm_mod.general_grouped_gemm_for_grouped_tensor(weights, grouped_x, out, layout=layout)
+        return out.rowwise_data
+
+    def reference():
+        swizzle_cache(False)
+        ref = gemm(make_out()).clone()
+        swizzle_cache(True)
+        return ref
+
+    swizzle_cache(False)
+    ref_out = make_out()
+    num_ref = _swizzle_kernel_count(lambda: gemm(ref_out))
+    swizzle_cache(True)
+
+    # The first call marks the weights; the post-all-gather refresh builds the views.
+    gemm(make_out())
+    assert all(getattr(w, "_gsw_wanted", False) for w in weights)
+    tensor_utils.post_all_gather_processing(weights)
+    assert all(getattr(w, "_gsw_view", None) is not None for w in weights)
+    out = make_out()
+    num_cached = _swizzle_kernel_count(lambda: gemm(out))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.rowwise_data, ref_out.rowwise_data, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert 0 < num_ref and num_cached < num_ref, (num_ref, num_cached)
+
+    # The refresh writes in place, so results follow the weights.
+    _update_weights(weights)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(gemm(make_out()), reference(), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    # A captured CUDA graph reads the refreshed scales on replay.
+    static_out = make_out()
+    gemm(static_out)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        gemm(static_out)
+    _update_weights(weights)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(static_out.rowwise_data, reference(), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_swizzle_pack_discrete_follows_param_gather(swizzle_cache, monkeypatch):
+    calls = []
+
+    def fake_pack(datas, scales, fmt, device):
+        calls.append(fmt)
+        return object()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        tex.grouped_mlp_experimental,
+        "swizzle_scales_and_pack_ptrs_for_discrete_weights",
+        fake_pack,
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(grouped_mlp_mod, "_DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE", {})
+    datas = [torch.empty(16, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)]
+    scales = [torch.empty(16, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)]
+    pack = grouped_mlp_mod._swizzle_pack_discrete
+
+    first = pack(datas, scales, "nvfp4", "cuda")
+    assert pack(datas, scales, "nvfp4", "cuda") is first
+    assert pack(datas, scales, "mxfp8_rowwise", "cuda") is not first
+    assert len(calls) == 2
+
+    tensor_utils.post_all_gather_processing([])
+    assert pack(datas, scales, "nvfp4", "cuda") is not first
+    assert len(calls) == 3
+
+    swizzle_cache(False)
+    pack(datas, scales, "nvfp4", "cuda")
+    pack(datas, scales, "nvfp4", "cuda")
+    assert len(calls) == 5

inline_comments.body: **Graphs read old weight scales** With `NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE=1`, warming up the fused grouped MLP before capturing a compute-only CUDA graph makes this branch return cached scales without capturing a swizzle. After weights change through `post_all_gather_processing`, replay still reads the old scales, producing wrong outputs and gradients. The host-side generation check does not run during replay, and the gather hook only refreshes the separate `_gsw_view` buffers. Refresh the buffers used by the captured MLP in place, or keep the swizzle in the graph. Add a replay test using the real fused MLP path; the mocked helper test cannot catch this. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch tensor and operator abstractions](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-tensors-and-ops.md)

+def _swizzle_pack_discrete(datas, scales, fmt, device):
+    """``swizzle_scales_and_pack_ptrs_for_discrete_weights``, cached until the weights change.

+    With ``NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE=1``, expert weights are assumed to change only at a
+    parameter all-gather (``post_all_gather_processing``), so the swizzled scales and packed
+    pointer arrays are reused by every microbatch until the next one. In a CUDA graph that
+    also captures the all-gather, the first use after it is captured and recomputes the
+    cached buffers on every replay.
+    """
+    fn = tex.grouped_mlp_experimental.swizzle_scales_and_pack_ptrs_for_discrete_weights
+    if not nvfp4_weight_swizzle_cache_enabled():

+    key = (

+        tuple(t.data_ptr() for t in scales),
+    )
+    hit = _DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE.get(key)
+    if hit is not None and hit[0] == gen:
+        return hit[1]

inline_comments.body: **Unused GPU buffers stay alive** `_DISCRETE_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE` keeps every distinct pointer key for the life of the process. Each value owns GPU scale and pointer buffers, but no entry is removed when its weights die. The fused MLP also calls this helper for BF16 expert weights that it quantizes afresh each forward. New allocation addresses leave old GPU buffers retained, including after a model is deleted. Tie entries to the owning weights or otherwise bound and clean up the cache without breaking captured graphs.

Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The opt\-in cache affects PyTorch GEMM workflows that use discrete weights\. Fix the fused grouped MLP's stale scales during graph replay before merging.

Findings

1.  **Graphs read old weight scales** ▶ 2.  **Unused GPU buffers stay alive** ▶

Summary

Adds opt-in caching through `NVTE_NVFP4_WEIGHT_SWIZZLE_CACHE` to avoid repeatedly swizzling gathered NVFP4 weight scales. - GEMMs reuse swizzled NVFP4 scales after each parameter gather. - Fused grouped MLPs reuse packed pointers for discrete weights.
